# Your own movie on the screen

A movie drawing gives your mod its own AS3 interface on any screen part. Use `CMFDraw(provider, anchor, id, 'movie')`, set `src` to `swf/<your folder>/<name>.swf`, and place it with the normal box keys. Use `mapSpace` and `cmfMapSpace` for a movie drawn in map coordinates instead. Keep ids and paths under your own folder name.

## Entry and data

Implement `cmfScreen(data:Object, map:Object):Boolean`. Return true after accepting the entry. `data.id` is the drawing id; `data.text` contains your text keys, `data.number` your numeric keys, and `data.keys` retains the earlier compatible typing. Pass player-facing words from your string tables rather than hard-coding them in AS3. A missing or failed entry releases the loader and any acquired input.

```actionscript
public function cmfScreen(data:Object, liveMap:Object):Boolean
{
    this.map = liveMap;
    this.id = String(data.id);
    caption.text = String(data.text.caption);
    return true;
}
```

The following original example assumes your MovieClip declares `map:Object`, `id:String`, and a `caption:TextField` it creates itself. It uses the game's bubbling event class without shipping a copy:

```actionscript
var GameEventClass:Class = getDefinitionByName("red.core.events.GameEvent") as Class;
dispatchEvent(new GameEventClass("callGameEvent", "OnCMFMovieEvent",
    [id, "picked", String(pin.id)], true, true));
```

CMF validates the live movie holder and drawing owner, then forwards three strings to `CMFCore.OnMovieEvent(menu, provider, id, eventName, value):bool`. Wrap that core hook and preserve `wrappedMethod`'s result for another provider. There is no `map.event` API.

## Map data and controls

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `map.pins` | Lazy cached array for the current completed pin build, including added and late pins. Reading it asks for the snapshot; a movie that never reads it causes no pin traversal. Pending builds return an empty list. A tab or filter change makes the next read return a new array, so compare the array itself to notice it. |
| Pin descriptor | `id` uint, `type`, `tag`, `label`, `x`, `y`, `tracked`, `area`, `shown`. Coordinates are world coordinates; tag text is empty unless CMF knows its typed name. Id 0 never tag-matches. `shown` is false while the current tab or filters hide the pin; list only shown pins if your list should follow them. |
| `map.area` | The shown area's typed journal name. |
| `map.zoom` | Actual map scale. |
| `map.view` | `x`, `y` map translation; `worldX`, `worldY` world centre; `zoom` scale. |
| `map.player` | Player world x/y, or null if unavailable. |
| `map.center(x,y,zoom,seconds)` | Centres through the game's coordinate conversion and actual zoom limits. Finite coordinates, positive zoom and nonnegative seconds are required. Mouse dragging cancels only this movie's centring tween. |
| `map.selectPin(id)` | Selects a descriptor's numeric id, or a tag text CMF already knows. Missing ids and unknown text do nothing; unknown text is logged once per provider/tag. |
| `map.lockPan(on)` | Pauses keyboard/pad panning while this live movie holds the lock. Zoom and pointer dragging keep working. |
| `map.showArea(area)` | Requests a different typed journal area, the name `map.area` and `OnMapAreaReady` use (for example `AN_NMLandNovigrad`, `AN_Skellige_ArdSkellig`); an unknown name logs `movie showArea unknown area=<name>`. Velen and Novigrad share one map; requesting the current map never reloads it. `OnMapAreaReady(menu,area)` fires when the new list and panel build are both ready. |
| `map.highlightPin(id,style)` | Temporary `pin` look keys for that pin; restores its previous look on release. `map.highlightPin(id,null)` takes that pin's temporary look back at once. |
| `map.noSpread(id)` | Keeps that id out of a spread while the movie owns it. |
| `map.focus(on)` | Acquires keys/pad only if the drawing set `focus` 1, or releases them with false. |

Prefer descriptor numeric ids. For known text tags, supply the typed name through a tag claim, an added pin, a style target or `CMFDeclareTag(provider, tag)`. Never convert an arbitrary id back into a name.

## Focus and cleanup

Set the drawing's `focus` key to 1 before calling `map.focus(true)`. Your `handleInput(event)` then receives the game's key/pad event first. Handle its down/up/hold values consistently and provide a visible way to call `map.focus(false)`. Taking or returning focus clears held pan and zoom input locally. A focused movie does not capture the mouse outside its own drawn area: native hover, clicks, right click and dragging continue there, including core pin-click hooks.

Hiding a movie or one of its display parents releases its focus, pan lock, centring and temporary pin effects. Its loader may stay ready, but callbacks and data requests are inactive while hidden. Showing it again calls `cmfScreen` again with the live map, but does not restore controls automatically; request them again explicitly. A key press consumed by the movie keeps its release, so returning focus does not also trigger a map action.

Removal, ownership loss, load failure, area change and map close always release focus, pan locks, temporary highlights and spread exclusions. Retained callbacks from an old facade are inert. Remove your own frame/listener/timer work when your clip leaves the stage; keep providers' persistence in their own scripts. Static/offline checks do not establish engine loading or controller acceptance.
